content.text:
## Repository hygiene report

**Starting state (what I found before touching anything):**
- Git history already existed: one commit, `fa71ea1` ("chore: initial import"), author SammyP, dated today.
- `.gitignore` at that commit already contained `.env` and `db/*.db` / `db/*.db-*` — contrary to the task's premise that `.env` wasn't ignored, it already was. `git ls-files` confirmed `.env` was never tracked (only `.env.example` was), and `db/lumen.db` was untracked too.
- `.claude/settings.json` hooks (UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse/Stop/SessionEnd → `ai-log.mjs`) and all `.claude/skills/*` files were present and unchanged — logging was never disabled.
- `data/` and `services/maintenance-api/` were untouched (the repo's own `.claude/settings.json` even hard-denies edits to them).

**Gap I found and corrected:**
`db/*.db` only ignores `.db` files inside `db/`, but `DB_PATH` is a configurable env var in all three places that open the database (`backend-ts/src/db.ts:6`, `backend-go/internal/config/config.go:41`, `scripts/seed.mjs:10`) — so a custom path outside `db/` wouldn't have been caught. I also hadn't accounted for other local env variants (`.env.local`, etc.). Updated [.gitignore](Lumen-equipment-challenge/.gitignore):

```
node_modules/
dist/
*.db
*.db-*
backend-go/bin/
.DS_Store
.idea
.env
.env.*
!.env.example
```

**Verification actually run (not just claimed):**
```bash
git check-ignore -v .env                 # → matched by .gitignore:8
git check-ignore -v .env.local           # → matched by .gitignore:9 (.env.*)
git check-ignore -v .env.example         # → NOT ignored (confirmed OK)
git check-ignore -v db/lumen.db          # → matched by *.db
git check-ignore -v backend-ts/test.db   # → matched by *.db (new coverage)
git check-ignore -v db/lumen.db-wal      # → matched by *.db-*
git diff --cached --name-only | grep -E '(^|/)\.env$|\.db$'   # → none found
git diff --cached | grep -niE '(api[_-]?key\s*=|secret\s*=|password\s*=|-----BEGIN)'  # → no matches
git grep -nIi -E '(api[_-]?key|secret|password|token|private[_-]?key|BEGIN [A-Z]+ PRIVATE KEY)' -- .   # tracked snapshot — only placeholders (fc_test_key, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=, code referencing env var names), no real secrets
grep -nIi -E '(api[_-]?key|secret|password|BEGIN [A-Z]+ PRIVATE KEY|bearer)' .ai-log/events.jsonl        # only logs my own prompt text, no secrets
```

1	# RTS Labs Engineering Challenge: Lumen Builders Equipment Scheduling
2	
3	Welcome, and thanks for spending time on this.
4	
5	You're joining an RTS Labs engagement as the consultant engineer. Our client, **Lumen Builders**, is a fictional mid-size general contractor. They have a scheduling problem that's costing them real money. A previous contractor started building a replacement for their spreadsheet and then left. You're picking it up.
6	
7	**This challenge is used for every level, from early-career to principal.** Nobody is expected to finish everything. Pick the depth that shows your best thinking. A small, correct, well-reasoned submission beats a large, shaky one.
8	
9	**AI tools are expected and encouraged.** This repo is set up for [Claude Code](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code) with project skills and automatic logging of your session. We care much more about **how you think, decide and direct the tools** than about how many lines get written.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 1. The client
14	
15	Lumen runs **12 active jobsites** across Virginia, North Carolina and Tennessee. They share a fleet of about **60 pieces of heavy equipment**: mobile and tower cranes, excavators, dozers, lifts and telehandlers. Some of it requires a certified operator.
16	
17	Today everything is scheduled in a shared Excel workbook. Here is what we heard in discovery.
18	
19	> **Dana Whitaker, Director of Operations**
20	> "Last month a 90-ton crane went to Short Pump while the steel crew at Riverside stood around for two days. That's about $38k in idle labor, and it happens every month or two. I want one place where anyone can see what's actually free."
21	> "The number one complaint is equipment that looks available in the sheet but is actually in the shop. The shop uses FleetCare for maintenance, and nobody checks it."
22	> "Honestly, tentative bookings shouldn't block anything. People put tentatives on everything 'just in case'."
23	
24	> **Marcus Bell, Superintendent (Riverside, Scott's Addition, James River Bridge)**
25	> "I'm checking this from a truck or a lift, on my phone, with gloves on and sun on the screen. If it's fiddly, nobody will use it."
26	> "You can't move a crane across town in zero minutes. Figure half a day between sites, minimum."
27	> "If two of my foremen grab the same excavator, fine, first one wins. But tell the second guy *right away*, not when the machine doesn't show up."
28	> "If I put a tentative on the crane, it's because I need it. Don't let somebody take it out from under me."
29	
30	> **Priya Nair, Safety Manager**
31	> "Nobody operates a crane, dozer or lift without a current certification. If someone's cert expires in the middle of a booking, that's an OSHA problem, and it has happened."
32	> "Operator records come from HR. They have personal information in them. Only people who need it should see it."
33	
34	> **Leo Park, IT Manager**
35	> "We're a Microsoft 365 shop. Eventually everyone should sign in with their work account (Entra ID). Subcontractors get guest accounts."
36	> "FleetCare is a vendor system. Their API is slow and goes down. We can't change it, and they rate-limit us."
37	> "We'll probably host in Azure. Please don't make me run Kubernetes."
38	
39	### Users and roles
40	
41	Demo users live in `data/users.json`. Lumen hasn't fully defined permissions yet. This is what we know:
42	
43	| Role | What we know |
44	|---|---|
45	| `ops_director` | Sees and manages everything. |
46	| `superintendent` | Runs one or more sites and manages equipment bookings for them. |
47	| `foreman` | Works at specific sites and requests or books equipment for them. |
48	| `safety_manager` | Oversees operator certifications company-wide. |
49	| `subcontractor` | An outside company working on a site. Needs to see the equipment schedule for their site. |
50	
51	Where the rules are unclear, **make a reasonable call and write it down**, or list it as a question you'd take back to the client.
52	
53	---
54	
55	## 2. What's in the repo
56	
57	```
58	frontend/                  React + TypeScript (Vite)
59	backend-ts/                TypeScript API (Express 5, node:sqlite)   ← pick ONE backend
60	backend-go/                Go API (net/http, modernc sqlite)         ←
61	db/schema.sql              Current schema (from the previous contractor)
62	data/                      Raw exports: sites, equipment, operators, bookings, users,
63	                           foreman_messages.jsonl (for Part 3D)
64	services/maintenance-api/  Mock of FleetCare, the vendor maintenance API (don't modify)
65	scripts/                   seed.mjs, dev-token.mjs
66	docs/plan/                 Your plans + PROGRESS.md
67	docs/decisions/            Your architecture decision records (ADRs)
68	docs/ai-log/               Exports from non-Claude AI tools, if used
69	.claude/                   Claude Code skills + logging hooks
70	CLAUDE.md                  Context for AI agents
71	SUBMISSION.md              Fill this in at the end
72	```
73	
74	Both backends implement the same single endpoint, `GET /api/equipment/availability`. **Choose one** (TypeScript or Go) and feel free to delete the other. You may switch from SQLite to Postgres (`docker compose up postgres`), but you don't have to.
75	
76	The existing code *runs*. Whether it's *right* is another matter. **Treat it like any codebase you inherit on a client project.**
77	
78	## 3. Getting started
79	
80	Prerequisites: **Node 22.13+** (always needed), and **Go 1.22+** only if you choose the Go backend. Docker is optional.
81	
82	```bash
83	git init && git add -A && git commit -m "chore: initial import"   # commit history is part of your submission
84	[ -f .env ] || cp .env.example .env
85	npm run setup               # installs frontend + backend-ts deps and seeds SQLite
86	
87	# in separate terminals
88	npm run mock                # FleetCare mock on :4010  (CHAOS=off npm run mock for a calm version)
89	npm run dev:ts              # or: cd backend-go && go mod tidy && go run ./cmd/api
90	npm run dev:web             # http://localhost:5173
91	
92	npm run token -- --list     # demo users
93	npm run token -- u-sup-01   # mint a dev JWT; paste it into the web app
94	```
95	
96	Try the API directly:
97	
98	```bash
99	TOKEN=$(npm run -s token -- u-for-01)
100	curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
101	  "http://localhost:8080/api/equipment/availability?type=mobile_crane&start=2026-10-01&end=2026-10-31" | jq
102	```
103	
104	**If you're using Claude Code**, start it from the repo root. The skills in `.claude/skills/` (`plan-first`, `decision-record`, `write-tests`, `security-review`, `checkpoint`, `submission`) are there to help you work the way we work on client projects. Using them is optional. Directing your agent well is what we're looking for.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## 4. The challenge
109	
110	### Part 0: Understand and plan (required)
111	
112	- Read the code, schema and data. Run the app.
113	- Write a plan in `docs/plan/01-<slug>.md`. The template and the `plan-first` skill will help.
114	- Make a list of **problems you find in the inherited code and data**, ranked by what matters most to Lumen. You don't have to fix them all. Show us you see them and can prioritise.
115	
116	### Part 1: Trustworthy availability (required)
117	
118	Make **"what equipment is free for these dates?"** something a superintendent can trust.
119	
120	- The `GET /api/equipment/availability` results should be **correct**, taking into account existing bookings and FleetCare maintenance windows.
121	- The endpoint should behave sensibly **when FleetCare is slow, down or rate-limiting**. Decide what "sensibly" means for Lumen and explain it.
122	- Users should see only what their role and sites allow.
123	- The UI should work for Marcus: on a phone, and **accessible**. It needs clear loading, empty and error states.
124	- Include tests that give you, and us, confidence.
125	
126	### Part 2: Reserve equipment (expected for mid-level and above)
127	
128	Add **`POST /api/reservations`** (and whatever else you need) so a user can book a piece of equipment for a site and a time range.
129	
130	- Two people booking the same equipment for overlapping times **must not both succeed**, even at the same instant.
131	- If the equipment requires a certified operator, the assigned operator's certification must be valid for the whole booking.
132	- Enforce who may book what.
133	- Return errors a client can act on.
134	- The UI for this can be minimal. The API and its guarantees matter more.
135	
136	### Part 3: Deep dive (pick at least one if you're senior or above; optional for everyone else)
137	
138	- **A. Prove the concurrency guarantee.** Write a test that fires many simultaneous reservation requests and shows exactly one wins. Explain the mechanism you rely on, and how it would change on Postgres or with multiple API instances.
139	- **B. Production readiness.** Add observability that would let you run this for Lumen: structured logs, request correlation, metrics on FleetCare latency and errors, health and readiness checks, and an audit trail of who booked or changed what. Tell us what you'd alert on and why.
140	- **C. Data and scale.** Redesign the schema properly and migrate the messy spreadsheet data into it (dates, time zones, asset tags, certifications). Then write a short design for about 10× scale: 120 sites, 600 assets, and possibly multiple client companies on one deployment. Cover indexes, caching and the FleetCare rate limit.
141	- **D. AI stretch goal: foreman text requests.** Foremen text requests like *"need a 90 ton crane at riverside tues thru thurs next week"*. Build a feature that turns a message into a **draft** reservation for a human to confirm. `data/foreman_messages.jsonl` has 24 labelled examples. Use it to build an **evaluation harness** and report your scores. Consider prompt injection, permissions, personal data sent to the model, cost and latency, and how you'd monitor quality over time. (A stubbed or mocked model is acceptable if you don't have an API key. We care most about the design and the eval.)
142	
143	---
144	
145	## 5. What to submit
146	
147	A git repository (or zip of one) that includes:
148	
149	1. **Your code**, with a commit history that shows how you worked.
150	2. **`SUBMISSION.md`**, filled in. This is important.
151	3. **`docs/plan/`** and **`docs/decisions/`**: your plans, progress log and ADRs.
152	4. **`.ai-log/`**: this is generated automatically if you use Claude Code. If you use other AI tools, put exports in `docs/ai-log/`. See `docs/ai-log/README.md`.
153	
154	Please **don't commit secrets** or local database files.
155	
156	## 6. Ground rules
157	
158	- Use any libraries, frameworks or AI tools you like.
159	- Don't modify `data/` or `services/maintenance-api/`. Treat them as the client's data and a vendor's system.
160	- Questions? Email us, or make an assumption, write it down and keep going. Both are fine, and how you handle ambiguity is part of what we look at.
161	- **Stop at 4 hours.** Unfinished work plus a clear "what I'd do next" is a normal, good outcome.
162	- If you need an accommodation (more time, a different format, anything else), just tell us. It won't affect your evaluation.
163	
164	## 7. How we'll evaluate
165	
166	We're not counting features. Across your code, docs, commits and AI log, we look at:
167	
168	- **Understanding the problem**: did you solve Lumen's problem, not just the ticket?
169	- **Technical judgement**: what you prioritised, what you deliberately didn't do, and why.
170	- **Architecture**: separation of concerns, abstractions, data modelling, and data flow from browser to database.
171	- **Correctness and resilience**: edge cases, failure handling, concurrency.
172	- **Security**: authentication, authorization, and handling of sensitive data.
173	- **Quality**: tests, readability, accessibility.
174	- **Delivery**: plan, commits, documentation, SDLC habits.
175	- **Working with AI**: how you directed, verified and corrected your tools.
176	
177	Afterwards there's a **45-minute conversation**. You'll walk us through your work, and we'll explore a few "what if" extensions together. No trick questions.
178	
179	Good luck, and have fun with it.

1	# RTS Labs Engineering Challenge: Lumen Builders Equipment Scheduling
2	
3	Welcome, and thanks for spending time on this.
4	
5	You're joining an RTS Labs engagement as the consultant engineer. Our client, **Lumen Builders**, is a fictional mid-size general contractor. They have a scheduling problem that's costing them real money. A previous contractor started building a replacement for their spreadsheet and then left. You're picking it up.
6	
7	**This challenge is used for every level, from early-career to principal.** Nobody is expected to finish everything. Pick the depth that shows your best thinking. A small, correct, well-reasoned submission beats a large, shaky one.
8	
9	**AI tools are expected and encouraged.** This repo is set up for [Claude Code](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code) with project skills and automatic logging of your session. We care much more about **how you think, decide and direct the tools** than about how many lines get written.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 1. The client
14	
15	Lumen runs **12 active jobsites** across Virginia, North Carolina and Tennessee. They share a fleet of about **60 pieces of heavy equipment**: mobile and tower cranes, excavators, dozers, lifts and telehandlers. Some of it requires a certified operator.
16	
17	Today everything is scheduled in a shared Excel workbook. Here is what we heard in discovery.
18	
19	> **Dana Whitaker, Director of Operations**
20	> "Last month a 90-ton crane went to Short Pump while the steel crew at Riverside stood around for two days. That's about $38k in idle labor, and it happens every month or two. I want one place where anyone can see what's actually free."
21	> "The number one complaint is equipment that looks available in the sheet but is actually in the shop. The shop uses FleetCare for maintenance, and nobody checks it."
22	> "Honestly, tentative bookings shouldn't block anything. People put tentatives on everything 'just in case'."
23	
24	> **Marcus Bell, Superintendent (Riverside, Scott's Addition, James River Bridge)**
25	> "I'm checking this from a truck or a lift, on my phone, with gloves on and sun on the screen. If it's fiddly, nobody will use it."
26	> "You can't move a crane across town in zero minutes. Figure half a day between sites, minimum."
27	> "If two of my foremen grab the same excavator, fine, first one wins. But tell the second guy *right away*, not when the machine doesn't show up."
28	> "If I put a tentative on the crane, it's because I need it. Don't let somebody take it out from under me."
29	
30	> **Priya Nair, Safety Manager**
31	> "Nobody operates a crane, dozer or lift without a current certification. If someone's cert expires in the middle of a booking, that's an OSHA problem, and it has happened."
32	> "Operator records come from HR. They have personal information in them. Only people who need it should see it."
33	
34	> **Leo Park, IT Manager**
35	> "We're a Microsoft 365 shop. Eventually everyone should sign in with their work account (Entra ID). Subcontractors get guest accounts."
36	> "FleetCare is a vendor system. Their API is slow and goes down. We can't change it, and they rate-limit us."
37	> "We'll probably host in Azure. Please don't make me run Kubernetes."
38	
39	### Users and roles
40	
41	Demo users live in `data/users.json`. Lumen hasn't fully defined permissions yet. This is what we know:
42	
43	| Role | What we know |
44	|---|---|
45	| `ops_director` | Sees and manages everything. |
46	| `superintendent` | Runs one or more sites and manages equipment bookings for them. |
47	| `foreman` | Works at specific sites and requests or books equipment for them. |
48	| `safety_manager` | Oversees operator certifications company-wide. |
49	| `subcontractor` | An outside company working on a site. Needs to see the equipment schedule for their site. |
50	
51	Where the rules are unclear, **make a reasonable call and write it down**, or list it as a question you'd take back to the client.
52	
53	---
54	
55	## 2. What's in the repo
56	
57	```
58	frontend/                  React + TypeScript (Vite)
59	backend-ts/                TypeScript API (Express 5, node:sqlite)   ← pick ONE backend
60	backend-go/                Go API (net/http, modernc sqlite)         ←
61	db/schema.sql              Current schema (from the previous contractor)
62	data/                      Raw exports: sites, equipment, operators, bookings, users,
63	                           foreman_messages.jsonl (for Part 3D)
64	services/maintenance-api/  Mock of FleetCare, the vendor maintenance API (don't modify)
65	scripts/                   seed.mjs, dev-token.mjs
66	docs/plan/                 Your plans + PROGRESS.md
67	docs/decisions/            Your architecture decision records (ADRs)
68	docs/ai-log/               Exports from non-Claude AI tools, if used
69	.claude/                   Claude Code skills + logging hooks
70	CLAUDE.md                  Context for AI agents
71	SUBMISSION.md              Fill this in at the end
72	```
73	
74	Both backends implement the same single endpoint, `GET /api/equipment/availability`. **Choose one** (TypeScript or Go) and feel free to delete the other. You may switch from SQLite to Postgres (`docker compose up postgres`), but you don't have to.
75	
76	The existing code *runs*. Whether it's *right* is another matter. **Treat it like any codebase you inherit on a client project.**
77	
78	## 3. Getting started
79	
80	Prerequisites: **Node 22.13+** (always needed), and **Go 1.22+** only if you choose the Go backend. Docker is optional.
81	
82	```bash
83	git init && git add -A && git commit -m "chore: initial import"   # commit history is part of your submission
84	[ -f .env ] || cp .env.example .env
85	npm run setup               # installs frontend + backend-ts deps and seeds SQLite
86	
87	# in separate terminals
88	npm run mock                # FleetCare mock on :4010  (CHAOS=off npm run mock for a calm version)
89	npm run dev:ts              # or: cd backend-go && go mod tidy && go run ./cmd/api
90	npm run dev:web             # http://localhost:5173
91	
92	npm run token -- --list     # demo users
93	npm run token -- u-sup-01   # mint a dev JWT; paste it into the web app
94	```
95	
96	Try the API directly:
97	
98	```bash
99	TOKEN=$(npm run -s token -- u-for-01)
100	curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
101	  "http://localhost:8080/api/equipment/availability?type=mobile_crane&start=2026-10-01&end=2026-10-31" | jq
102	```
103	
104	**If you're using Claude Code**, start it from the repo root. The skills in `.claude/skills/` (`plan-first`, `decision-record`, `write-tests`, `security-review`, `checkpoint`, `submission`) are there to help you work the way we work on client projects. Using them is optional. Directing your agent well is what we're looking for.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## 4. The challenge
109	
110	### Part 0: Understand and plan (required)
111	
112	- Read the code, schema and data. Run the app.
113	- Write a plan in `docs/plan/01-<slug>.md`. The template and the `plan-first` skill will help.
114	- Make a list of **problems you find in the inherited code and data**, ranked by what matters most to Lumen. You don't have to fix them all. Show us you see them and can prioritise.
115	
116	### Part 1: Trustworthy availability (required)
117	
118	Make **"what equipment is free for these dates?"** something a superintendent can trust.
119	
120	- The `GET /api/equipment/availability` results should be **correct**, taking into account existing bookings and FleetCare maintenance windows.
121	- The endpoint should behave sensibly **when FleetCare is slow, down or rate-limiting**. Decide what "sensibly" means for Lumen and explain it.
122	- Users should see only what their role and sites allow.
123	- The UI should work for Marcus: on a phone, and **accessible**. It needs clear loading, empty and error states.
124	- Include tests that give you, and us, confidence.
125	
126	### Part 2: Reserve equipment (expected for mid-level and above)
127	
128	Add **`POST /api/reservations`** (and whatever else you need) so a user can book a piece of equipment for a site and a time range.
129	
130	- Two people booking the same equipment for overlapping times **must not both succeed**, even at the same instant.
131	- If the equipment requires a certified operator, the assigned operator's certification must be valid for the whole booking.
132	- Enforce who may book what.
133	- Return errors a client can act on.
134	- The UI for this can be minimal. The API and its guarantees matter more.
135	
136	### Part 3: Deep dive (pick at least one if you're senior or above; optional for everyone else)
137	
138	- **A. Prove the concurrency guarantee.** Write a test that fires many simultaneous reservation requests and shows exactly one wins. Explain the mechanism you rely on, and how it would change on Postgres or with multiple API instances.
139	- **B. Production readiness.** Add observability that would let you run this for Lumen: structured logs, request correlation, metrics on FleetCare latency and errors, health and readiness checks, and an audit trail of who booked or changed what. Tell us what you'd alert on and why.
140	- **C. Data and scale.** Redesign the schema properly and migrate the messy spreadsheet data into it (dates, time zones, asset tags, certifications). Then write a short design for about 10× scale: 120 sites, 600 assets, and possibly multiple client companies on one deployment. Cover indexes, caching and the FleetCare rate limit.
141	- **D. AI stretch goal: foreman text requests.** Foremen text requests like *"need a 90 ton crane at riverside tues thru thurs next week"*. Build a feature that turns a message into a **draft** reservation for a human to confirm. `data/foreman_messages.jsonl` has 24 labelled examples. Use it to build an **evaluation harness** and report your scores. Consider prompt injection, permissions, personal data sent to the model, cost and latency, and how you'd monitor quality over time. (A stubbed or mocked model is acceptable if you don't have an API key. We care most about the design and the eval.)
142	
143	---
144	
145	## 5. What to submit
146	
147	A git repository (or zip of one) that includes:
148	
149	1. **Your code**, with a commit history that shows how you worked.
150	2. **`SUBMISSION.md`**, filled in. This is important.
151	3. **`docs/plan/`** and **`docs/decisions/`**: your plans, progress log and ADRs.
152	4. **`.ai-log/`**: this is generated automatically if you use Claude Code. If you use other AI tools, put exports in `docs/ai-log/`. See `docs/ai-log/README.md`.
153	
154	Please **don't commit secrets** or local database files.
155	
156	## 6. Ground rules
157	
158	- Use any libraries, frameworks or AI tools you like.
159	- Don't modify `data/` or `services/maintenance-api/`. Treat them as the client's data and a vendor's system.
160	- Questions? Email us, or make an assumption, write it down and keep going. Both are fine, and how you handle ambiguity is part of what we look at.
161	- **Stop at 4 hours.** Unfinished work plus a clear "what I'd do next" is a normal, good outcome.
162	- If you need an accommodation (more time, a different format, anything else), just tell us. It won't affect your evaluation.
163	
164	## 7. How we'll evaluate
165	
166	We're not counting features. Across your code, docs, commits and AI log, we look at:
167	
168	- **Understanding the problem**: did you solve Lumen's problem, not just the ticket?
169	- **Technical judgement**: what you prioritised, what you deliberately didn't do, and why.
170	- **Architecture**: separation of concerns, abstractions, data modelling, and data flow from browser to database.
171	- **Correctness and resilience**: edge cases, failure handling, concurrency.
172	- **Security**: authentication, authorization, and handling of sensitive data.
173	- **Quality**: tests, readability, accessibility.
174	- **Delivery**: plan, commits, documentation, SDLC habits.
175	- **Working with AI**: how you directed, verified and corrected your tools.
176	
177	Afterwards there's a **45-minute conversation**. You'll walk us through your work, and we'll explore a few "what if" extensions together. No trick questions.
178	
179	Good luck, and have fun with it.

1	package auth

3	import (
4		"context"
5		"encoding/base64"
6		"encoding/json"
7		"net/http"
8		"strings"
9	)
10	
11	type User struct {
12		Sub     string   `json:"sub"`
13		Name    string   `json:"name"`
14		Role    string   `json:"role"`
15		SiteIDs []string `json:"site_ids"`
16	}
17	
18	type ctxKey struct{}
19	
20	// RequireAuth reads the user from the bearer token.
21	func RequireAuth(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
22		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
23			header := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
24			if header == "" {
25				http.Error(w, `{"error":"missing token"}`, http.StatusUnauthorized)
26				return
27			}
28			token := strings.TrimPrefix(header, "Bearer ")
29			parts := strings.Split(token, ".")
30			payload, _ := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(parts[1])
31			var u User
32			json.Unmarshal(payload, &u)
33			next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(context.WithValue(r.Context(), ctxKey{}, &u)))
34		})
35	}
36	
37	func UserFrom(r *http.Request) *User {
38		u, _ := r.Context().Value(ctxKey{}).(*User)
39		return u
40	}

6		"log"
7		"net/http"
8		"runtime/debug"
9	
10		"lumen/equipment-api/internal/auth"
11		"lumen/equipment-api/internal/handlers"
12	)
13	
14	func New() http.Handler {
15		mux := http.NewServeMux()
16		mux.HandleFunc("GET /healthz", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
17			w.Write([]byte(`{"ok":true}`))
18		})
19		mux.Handle("GET /api/equipment/availability", auth.RequireAuth(http.HandlerFunc(handlers.Availability)))
20	
21		return cors(logRequests(recoverErrors(mux)))
22	}
23	
24	func cors(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
25		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
26			w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")
27			w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Credentials", "true")
28			w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Headers", "*")
29			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
30		})
31	}
32	
33	func logRequests(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
34		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
35			h, _ := json.Marshal(r.Header)
36			log.Println(r.Method, r.URL.String(), string(h))
37			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
38		})
39	}
40	
41	func recoverErrors(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
42		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
43			defer func() {
44				if err := recover(); err != nil {
45					log.Println(err)
46					w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
47					w.WriteHeader(http.StatusInternalServerError)
48					json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(map[string]string{
49						"error": fmt.Sprint(err),
50						"stack": string(debug.Stack()),
51					})
52				}
53			}()
54			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
55		})
56	}

28		enc := base64.RawURLEncoding
29		h, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]string{"alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT"})
30		p, _ := json.Marshal(claims)
31		unsigned := enc.EncodeToString(h) + "." + enc.EncodeToString(p)
32		mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, []byte(os.Getenv("JWT_SECRET")))
33		mac.Write([]byte(unsigned))
34		return unsigned + "." + enc.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))
35	}

42		}
43	}

46		req := httptest.NewRequest("GET", "/api/equipment/availability?type=mobile_crane&start=2026-10-13&end=2026-10-15", nil)
47		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token(map[string]any{"sub": "u-ops-01", "role": "ops_director", "site_ids": []string{"*"}}))
48		rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
49		server.New().ServeHTTP(rec, req)
50	
51		if rec.Code != http.StatusOK {
52			t.Fatalf("expected 200, got %d: %s", rec.Code, rec.Body.String())
53		}
54		var body struct {
55			Data []map[string]any `json:"data"`
56		}
57		json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &body)
58		if len(body.Data) == 0 {
59			t.Fatal("expected some cranes")
60		}
61		for _, e := range body.Data {
62			if e["type"] != "mobile_crane" {

64			}
65		}

3	A stand-in for the third-party maintenance system Lumen's equipment shop uses. **Treat it as a vendor API you can't change.**
4	
5	```bash

8	```
9	
10	| Endpoint | Notes |
11	|---|---|
12	| `GET /v1/health` | No auth |
13	| `GET /v1/assets/:assetTag/maintenance` | One asset per call |
14	| `POST /v1/maintenance/batch` | `{ "asset_tags": [...] }`, max 25 per call |
15	
16	Auth: `X-Api-Key` header (see `.env.example`).
17	
18	Here's what the vendor's docs say, verbatim: *"Service is provided on a best-effort basis. Clients should expect intermittent errors and must respect rate limits (20 req / 10 s)."*
19	
20	Maintenance windows are returned as UTC timestamps. An asset is **not usable** during a window.

# FleetCare (mock)

A stand-in for the third-party maintenance system Lumen's equipment shop uses. **Treat it as a vendor API you can't change.**

```bash
npm run mock              # from repo root, chaos ON (realistic)
CHAOS=off npm run mock    # chaos off, for local UI work
```

| Endpoint | Notes |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/health` | No auth |
| `GET /v1/assets/:assetTag/maintenance` | One asset per call |
| `POST /v1/maintenance/batch` | `{ "asset_tags": [...] }`, max 25 per call |

Auth: `X-Api-Key` header (see `.env.example`).

Here's what the vendor's docs say, verbatim: *"Service is provided on a best-effort basis. Clients should expect intermittent errors and must respect rate limits (20 req / 10 s)."*

Maintenance windows are returned as UTC timestamps. An asset is **not usable** during a window.

1	# FleetCare (mock)
2	
3	A stand-in for the third-party maintenance system Lumen's equipment shop uses. **Treat it as a vendor API you can't change.**
4	
5	```bash
6	npm run mock              # from repo root, chaos ON (realistic)
7	CHAOS=off npm run mock    # chaos off, for local UI work
8	```
9	
10	| Endpoint | Notes |
11	|---|---|
12	| `GET /v1/health` | No auth |
13	| `GET /v1/assets/:assetTag/maintenance` | One asset per call |
14	| `POST /v1/maintenance/batch` | `{ "asset_tags": [...] }`, max 25 per call |
15	
16	Auth: `X-Api-Key` header (see `.env.example`).
17	
18	Here's what the vendor's docs say, verbatim: *"Service is provided on a best-effort basis. Clients should expect intermittent errors and must respect rate limits (20 req / 10 s)."*
19	
20	Maintenance windows are returned as UTC timestamps. An asset is **not usable** during a window.
21

---
name: write-tests
description: Use when adding or changing behaviour in backend-ts, backend-go or frontend. Enumerates cases first, then writes focused automated tests using this repo's tooling.
---

# Write tests

## 1. Enumerate before you write

Before writing any test code, produce a table of cases:

| # | Scenario | Input / setup | Expected | Why it matters |
|---|----------|---------------|----------|----------------|

Cover these categories, or state why one doesn't apply:
- Happy path
- Boundaries (empty, exactly-equal, first/last, limits)
- Invalid input
- Permissions (who must **not** be able to do or see this)
- External dependency failure
- Concurrency (two actors at once)
- Data quality (the seed data is a spreadsheet export)

Show the table to the human if the behaviour is ambiguous. Ambiguous cases are product questions.

## 2. Tooling

| Project | Runner | Command |
|---|---|---|
| backend-ts | vitest + supertest | `npm --prefix backend-ts test` |
| backend-go | `go test` | `cd backend-go && go test ./...` |
| frontend | vitest + Testing Library (jsdom) | `npm --prefix frontend test` |

## 3. Principles

- Tests must be deterministic and runnable offline. Don't depend on the FleetCare mock's random chaos. Inject a fake client or use `CHAOS=off` / `CHAOS_SEED`.
- Prefer testing through a public seam (HTTP handler, service function) over private internals.
- Each test sets up the data it needs. Tests that depend on whatever happens to be in the dev database are brittle, so flag them if you find them.
- A test that has never failed proves nothing. Where practical, see it fail first.
- Run the full suite before declaring done, and paste the summary line into your checkpoint.

---
name: security-review
description: Use before committing a feature or when asked to review code for security. Reviews the current diff (or named files) against a checklist and writes findings to docs/reviews/.
---

# Security review

## Scope

By default, review `git diff main...HEAD` plus any uncommitted changes. If the human names files, review those instead.

## Checklist

For each item, answer **OK / Issue / N/A**, with file:line evidence.

1. **Authentication**: are credentials and tokens actually verified (signature, expiry, issuer, audience)? Are there any code paths that skip it?
2. **Authorization**: is access checked per resource, not just per route? Can user A read or change user B's or site B's data?
3. **Input handling**: is every external input validated (type, range, size)? Are queries parameterized?
4. **Sensitive data**: what personal data (PII) or secrets are read? Are only the needed fields returned, per role? Is anything sensitive written to logs, errors, analytics or LLM prompts?
5. **Secrets management**: are there secrets in source, committed config, or client bundles? Does `.gitignore` cover them?
6. **Error handling**: do errors leak internals (stack traces, SQL, file paths) to clients?
7. **Transport and browser**: is the CORS policy intentional? Where are tokens stored on the client?
8. **Abuse and limits**: can someone request unbounded data, trigger expensive work, or overwhelm a downstream vendor?
9. **Dependencies**: are there new packages, and are they justified?
10. **AI-specific** (if an LLM is involved): prompt injection, output validation, data sent to third parties.

## Output

Write `docs/reviews/<date>-<slug>.md` with a table: `Severity (High/Med/Low) | Finding | Evidence | Recommendation | Status`. Then summarise the top three for the human. **Do not silently fix issues outside the current task's scope.** List them and let the human prioritise.

## Steps

5. **Chosen approach** and why. If the decision is significant or hard to reverse, also create an ADR with the `decision-record` skill.
6. **Task breakdown.** Small, ordered steps, each independently testable and committable.
7. **Test plan.** What proves this works? List the cases, including failure and edge cases.
8. **Risks / out of scope.** What you are deliberately *not* doing and why.

## Output

Save the plan to `docs/plan/NN-<short-slug>.md`, where NN is the next number. Use `docs/plan/TEMPLATE.md`.

1	---
2	name: write-tests
3	description: Use when adding or changing behaviour in backend-ts, backend-go or frontend. Enumerates cases first, then writes focused automated tests using this repo's tooling.
4	---
5	
6	# Write tests
7	
8	## 1. Enumerate before you write
9	
10	Before writing any test code, produce a table of cases:
11	
12	| # | Scenario | Input / setup | Expected | Why it matters |
13	|---|----------|---------------|----------|----------------|
14	
15	Cover these categories, or state why one doesn't apply:
16	- Happy path
17	- Boundaries (empty, exactly-equal, first/last, limits)
18	- Invalid input
19	- Permissions (who must **not** be able to do or see this)
20	- External dependency failure
21	- Concurrency (two actors at once)
22	- Data quality (the seed data is a spreadsheet export)
23	
24	Show the table to the human if the behaviour is ambiguous. Ambiguous cases are product questions.
25	
26	## 2. Tooling
27	
28	| Project | Runner | Command |
29	|---|---|---|
30	| backend-ts | vitest + supertest | `npm --prefix backend-ts test` |
31	| backend-go | `go test` | `cd backend-go && go test ./...` |
32	| frontend | vitest + Testing Library (jsdom) | `npm --prefix frontend test` |
33	
34	## 3. Principles
35	
36	- Tests must be deterministic and runnable offline. Don't depend on the FleetCare mock's random chaos. Inject a fake client or use `CHAOS=off` / `CHAOS_SEED`.
37	- Prefer testing through a public seam (HTTP handler, service function) over private internals.
38	- Each test sets up the data it needs. Tests that depend on whatever happens to be in the dev database are brittle, so flag them if you find them.
39	- A test that has never failed proves nothing. Where practical, see it fail first.
40	- Run the full suite before declaring done, and paste the summary line into your checkpoint.
41

1	---
2	name: security-review
3	description: Use before committing a feature or when asked to review code for security. Reviews the current diff (or named files) against a checklist and writes findings to docs/reviews/.
4	---
5	
6	# Security review
7	
8	## Scope
9	
10	By default, review `git diff main...HEAD` plus any uncommitted changes. If the human names files, review those instead.
11	
12	## Checklist
13	
14	For each item, answer **OK / Issue / N/A**, with file:line evidence.
15	
16	1. **Authentication**: are credentials and tokens actually verified (signature, expiry, issuer, audience)? Are there any code paths that skip it?
17	2. **Authorization**: is access checked per resource, not just per route? Can user A read or change user B's or site B's data?
18	3. **Input handling**: is every external input validated (type, range, size)? Are queries parameterized?
19	4. **Sensitive data**: what personal data (PII) or secrets are read? Are only the needed fields returned, per role? Is anything sensitive written to logs, errors, analytics or LLM prompts?
20	5. **Secrets management**: are there secrets in source, committed config, or client bundles? Does `.gitignore` cover them?
21	6. **Error handling**: do errors leak internals (stack traces, SQL, file paths) to clients?
22	7. **Transport and browser**: is the CORS policy intentional? Where are tokens stored on the client?
23	8. **Abuse and limits**: can someone request unbounded data, trigger expensive work, or overwhelm a downstream vendor?
24	9. **Dependencies**: are there new packages, and are they justified?
25	10. **AI-specific** (if an LLM is involved): prompt injection, output validation, data sent to third parties.
26	
27	## Output
28	
29	Write `docs/reviews/<date>-<slug>.md` with a table: `Severity (High/Med/Low) | Finding | Evidence | Recommendation | Status`. Then summarise the top three for the human. **Do not silently fix issues outside the current task's scope.** List them and let the human prioritise.
30

1	---
2	name: plan-first
3	description: Use before starting any non-trivial change in this repo (a new endpoint, a schema change, a refactor, any challenge Part). Produces a written plan in docs/plan/ before code is written, and keeps it updated as work proceeds.
4	---
5	
6	# Plan first
7	
8	Write down what you're going to do before any code gets written. The plan is a deliverable in its own right. Reviewers read it to see how the problem was understood.
9	
10	## Steps
11	
12	1. **Restate the problem** in 2–4 sentences, in the business's language (superintendents, foremen, cranes), not the code's.
13	2. **Read before proposing.** Look at the relevant code, schema and data files. Note anything surprising.
14	3. **List assumptions and open questions.** Mark each one as either:
15	   - *Assumed*: we'll proceed on this basis, and it's written down so it can be challenged.
16	   - *Blocking*: we need an answer first. Ask the human.
17	4. **Options.** Give at least two approaches for the core design decision, each with its trade-offs (complexity, correctness, performance, time).
18	5. **Chosen approach** and why. If the decision is significant or hard to reverse, also create an ADR with the `decision-record` skill.
19	6. **Task breakdown.** Small, ordered steps, each independently testable and committable.
20	7. **Test plan.** What proves this works? List the cases, including failure and edge cases.
21	8. **Risks / out of scope.** What you are deliberately *not* doing and why.
22	
23	## Output
24	
25	Save the plan to `docs/plan/NN-<short-slug>.md`, where NN is the next number. Use `docs/plan/TEMPLATE.md`.
26	
27	Present the plan to the human and **wait for approval** before implementing. If the human changes direction, update the plan: note what changed and why rather than silently rewriting it.
28	
29	As work proceeds, update the plan's `## Status log` section with dated one-line entries. When a plan is abandoned or replaced, set its status to `superseded` and link to the new plan. Never delete a plan.
30

1	---
2	name: decision-record
3	description: Use when making a significant or hard-to-reverse technical decision (database choice, concurrency strategy, auth approach, API shape, handling of a vendor outage, adopting an LLM). Writes a short Architecture Decision Record to docs/decisions/.
4	---
5	
6	# Architecture Decision Record
7	
8	1. Find the next number in `docs/decisions/` (they look like `0001-...md`).
9	2. Copy `docs/decisions/0000-template.md` to `docs/decisions/NNNN-<kebab-title>.md`.
10	3. Fill in the sections:
11	   - **Context**: the forces at play, including business constraints, not just technical ones.
12	   - **Options considered**: at least two, with honest pros and cons.
13	   - **Decision**: one paragraph.
14	   - **Consequences**: what gets easier, what gets harder, and what we would need to revisit (and at what scale or trigger).
15	4. Keep it under a page. Link it from the relevant plan in `docs/plan/`.
16	5. If a later decision reverses this one, don't edit history. Set this record to `Superseded by NNNN` and write a new one.
17

1	---
2	name: checkpoint
3	description: Use at natural stopping points (after finishing a task step, before a break, before switching approach, roughly every 30–45 minutes). Appends a short progress entry to docs/plan/PROGRESS.md and suggests a commit.

5	
6	# Checkpoint
7	
8	1. Run the relevant test suite(s) and capture the summary line.
9	2. Append an entry to `docs/plan/PROGRESS.md`:

11	```md
12	## <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM> — <one-line headline>

16	- **Next:** …
17	- **Open questions / risks:** …

19	
20	3. Suggest a conventional commit message for the work since the last checkpoint (`feat:`, `fix:`, `test:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`). Keep commits small and focused. Before committing, check that no secrets or local databases are staged.

content.text:
# Reconnaissance report: Lumen equipment scheduling system

No files changed. Mechanical checks were run via a throwaway script at `/private/tmp/claude-501/.../scratchpad/analyze2.mjs` (outside the repo, not committed). No `.env` contents were read. No real operator PII (names, phone, email, DOB, SSN, emergency contacts) appears below — only `operator_id`s, aggregate counts, and cert type/expiry.

---

## 1. End-to-end factual description

**Browser → API → DB, and FleetCare, as they exist today:**

1. **Frontend** ([frontend/src/App.tsx](Lumen-equipment-challenge/frontend/src/App.tsx)) is a single React component. Auth is "paste a dev JWT into a text box," stored in `localStorage` ([App.tsx:15,34-37](Lumen-equipment-challenge/frontend/src/App.tsx:15)). On every filter change it calls `GET /api/equipment/availability?type=&start=&end=` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` ([App.tsx:21-28](Lumen-equipment-challenge/frontend/src/App.tsx:21)) and renders the response into cards.
2. **Auth middleware**, identical in both backends, reads the bearer token, **base64-decodes the JWT payload segment and trusts it as-is — the signature is never checked** (TS: [backend-ts/src/auth.ts:24-26](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-ts/src/auth.ts:24); Go: [backend-go/internal/auth/auth.go:28-32](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-go/internal/auth/auth.go:28)). `scripts/dev-token.mjs` *does* sign correctly with `JWT_SECRET` ([scripts/dev-token.mjs:49-51](Lumen-equipment-challenge/scripts/dev-token.mjs:49)) — the signing side is fine, only the verifying side is missing.
3. **The availability handler** (TS: [backend-ts/src/routes/availability.ts](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-ts/src/routes/availability.ts); Go: [backend-go/internal/handlers/availability.go](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-go/internal/handlers/availability.go)) builds `SELECT * FROM equipment WHERE status='active'`, string-concatenating `type` directly into the SQL (TS:16, Go:21). For each equipment row it pulls **every** booking for that `asset_tag` with no status filter, and flags a conflict when `b.start_at >= start && b.end_at <= end` (TS:29, Go:40) — i.e. it only catches bookings fully **contained inside** the query window, not bookings that **overlap** it. There is **no FleetCare call anywhere** — both files have the identical comment `// TODO: check FleetCare for maintenance windows (Dana says this is the #1 complaint)` (TS:40, Go:53).
4. **Database**: SQLite, loaded by `scripts/seed.mjs` straight from the CSV/JSON in `data/` with no cleaning, type coercion, or validation ([seed.mjs:16-37](Lumen-equipment-challenge/scripts/seed.mjs:16)). Schema ([db/schema.sql](Lumen-equipment-challenge/db/schema.sql)) has **five tables, every column `TEXT`, and zero primary keys, foreign keys, `NOT NULL`, `UNIQUE`, `CHECK`, or indexes**.
5. **FleetCare** is a local mock ([services/maintenance-api/server.mjs](Lumen-equipment-challenge/services/maintenance-api/server.mjs)): `X-Api-Key` auth, 20 req/10s global rate limit, and (with `CHAOS=on`, the default) a 12% chance of 503, 8% chance of a 2.5–5s delay, 3% chance of a truncated JSON body, 2% chance of hanging 30s then 504. It is not called by either backend today, so none of this is currently exercised.
6. **CORS** on both backends is `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` combined with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` (TS: [app.ts:8-9](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-ts/src/app.ts:8); Go: [server.go:26-28](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-go/internal/server/server.go:26)) — an invalid/anti-pattern combination. Both also log full request headers, including the raw `Authorization` bearer token, to stdout on every request (TS: [app.ts:14-17](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-ts/src/app.ts:14); Go: [server.go:33-39](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-go/internal/server/server.go:33)), and both error handlers return `err.message` **and the stack trace** to the client on a 500 (TS: [app.ts:25-28](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-ts/src/app.ts:25); Go: [server.go:41-56](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-go/internal/server/server.go:41)).
7. The two backends are **functionally identical** — same bugs, same structure — so the TS-vs-Go choice doesn't change anything below.

---

## 2. Test inventory

| Suite | Tests | What they exercise | What they do **not** establish |
|---|---|---|---|
| `backend-ts/test/availability.test.ts` | 2 | 401 with no token; 200 + all-same-`type` when a validly-shaped token is sent | **Never asserts on the `available` or `conflict` fields at all.** Doesn't test auth *rejection* of a bad/forged token (can't — there's no verification to test). No site/role filtering (none exists). No FleetCare. No date/overlap correctness. No SQL-injection-safe input. No malformed-token handling. |
| `backend-go/internal/handlers/availability_test.go` | 2 | Same two cases, mirrored | Same gaps as TS. |
| `frontend/src/App.test.tsx` | 1 | Logged-out state shows the token input | No test renders the equipment list, loading state, error state, or filter interaction. No accessibility assertions. |
| Part 2 (`POST /api/reservations`) | 0 | — | Doesn't exist yet (expected — out of Part 0/1 scope). |

The most important gap: **no existing test would fail even if the overlap logic were completely inverted**, because neither availability test asserts on `available`/`conflict`. The two tests that exist use a date range (`2026-10-13`–`2026-10-15`) that happens not to intersect any of the bugs below, so "tests pass" does not mean "availability is correct."

---

## 3. Ranked problem register

Ordered as instructed: safety → double-booking → incorrect availability → authorization/PII → resilience → data quality → accessibility → maintainability. Severity reasoning, not dollar figures.

### A. Equipment safety

| # | Finding | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | **Maintenance/hazard state isn't checked at all.** FleetCare integration is a stub; a crane mid-repair shows as bookable. | TODO comments at [availability.ts:40](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-ts/src/routes/availability.ts:40) / [availability.go:53](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-go/internal/handlers/availability.go:53). This is Dana's stated #1 complaint, and it's unfixed in the "new" system too. |
| A2 | **Known hazards live only in a free-text `notes` field**, invisible unless a user clicks the card and reads an `alert()`. 11 of 60 equipment rows (18.3%) — including a tower crane (TC-002) and a mobile crane (MC-005), both cert-required — carry `"hydraulic leak reported 9/2 - check before use"`, and all 11 still have `status=active` so they pass the availability filter untouched. | Verified by grep: `grep -c "hydraulic leak" data/equipment.csv` → 11; [App.tsx:61](Lumen-equipment-challenge/frontend/src/App.tsx:61) shows notes only via `onClick → alert()`. |
| A3 | **No operator-certification enforcement exists anywhere** (expected — Part 2 isn't built), but the underlying data makes this nontrivial: 106 of 743 bookings (14.3%) are on cert-required equipment with **no operator assigned at all**, and cert expiry dates are stored in two incompatible formats, often mixed in the same field (see Data quality, below). Any cert check built on this data has to handle both problems. | Script output: `bookings on cert-required equipment with NO operator assigned: 106`. |

### B. Double-booking

| # | Finding | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | **The seed data already contains real double-bookings**, independent of any application bug: 18 pairs of **confirmed-vs-confirmed** bookings for the same asset with overlapping time ranges (plus 8 confirmed-vs-tentative, 6 tentative-vs-tentative, 3 involving a cancelled booking that don't count). This is Dana's crane-at-Short-Pump story, proven to already be happening, 18 times over, in the exported spreadsheet data the system was seeded from. | Script output: `confirmedVsConfirmed: 18`. Example: `EX-005` booked `BK-1111` (S07, 2026-11-08 07:00–15:00, confirmed) overlaps `BK-1303` (S11, 2026-11-07 07:00–2026-11-08 18:00, confirmed). |
| B2 | **No DB constraint of any kind prevents a new double-booking.** No unique index, no exclusion constraint, no transaction discipline — `db/schema.sql` has zero constraints on any table. | [db/schema.sql:48-58](Lumen-equipment-challenge/db/schema.sql:48). This is necessary context for Part 2 (not itself a Part 0/1 bug, since `POST /api/reservations` doesn't exist yet). |

### C. Incorrect availability (the stated Part 1 requirement)

This is where the most severe, stacked, mechanically-provable bugs live. Three independent defects compound:

| # | Finding | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | **Containment, not overlap.** `b.start_at >= start && b.end_at <= end` only matches bookings fully inside the query window. A booking that *spans* the query window is invisible. Worked example with real data: `BK-1005` books `MC-007` at S05 from `2026-11-15T11:00:00Z` to `2026-11-25T20:00:00Z` (confirmed). A superintendent querying availability for Nov 20–22 (squarely inside that booking) gets `b.start_at(Nov15) >= start(Nov20)` → **false**, so `MC-007` is reported **available** while it is actively on a 10-day confirmed booking. | [availability.ts:29](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-ts/src/routes/availability.ts:29) / [availability.go:40](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-go/internal/handlers/availability.go:40); `data/bookings.csv` row `BK-1005`. |
| C2 | **Date formats are heterogeneous and compared as raw strings.** `bookings.csv` uses 4 incompatible formats: `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` (594 of 743, 80%), ISO-with-`Z` (47, 6.3%), `MM/DD/YYYY` date-only (25, 3.4%), `MM/DD/YYYY hh:mm AM/PM` (77, 10.4%). The frontend sends plain `YYYY-MM-DD`. Verified: `"10/23/2026" >= "2026-10-01"` evaluates to **`false`** in JS (and identically in Go's `>=` on strings) purely because `'1' < '2'` lexicographically — the actual calendar order is irrelevant. This means **every one of the 102 bookings in the two `MM/DD/YYYY` formats (13.7% of all bookings) can never satisfy the start-side of the conflict check**, regardless of real overlap, so they can never block availability. | Script `node -e` verification above; format-bucket counts from `analyze2.mjs`. |
| C3 | **Asset-tag joins are exact-string, against a dirty foreign key.** `bookings.csv.asset_tag` doesn't reliably match `equipment.csv.asset_tag`: 35 bookings use lowercase tags (`ex-005`), 24 have stray whitespace (`"TH-005 "`), and **16 strip the hyphen entirely** (`DZ003`, `BL001`, `EX002`, `SL002`, `EX012`, `EX009`, `TH005`, `EX007`, `EX006`, `EX011`, `TC001`, `SL008`, `MC005`, `EX010`, plus 2 more — same equipment, just malformed). All 75 (10.1% of bookings) fail the backend's exact `WHERE asset_tag = ?` join and so are **never considered** for that equipment's conflict check at all. | Script output: `pure case mismatch: 35`, `whitespace padding: 24`, `TRULY UNKNOWN: 16` with the tag list; confirmed `seed.mjs` does no normalization on ingest ([seed.mjs:31-35](Lumen-equipment-challenge/scripts/seed.mjs:31)), so this reaches the database unchanged. |
| C4 | **Cancelled bookings still block.** There's no status filter in the query at all — a `status='cancelled'` booking (29 of 743, 3.9%) counts exactly like a confirmed one. | [availability.ts:22-24](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-ts/src/routes/availability.ts:22) — no `WHERE status != 'cancelled'` anywhere. |
| C5 | **Unbounded/missing query params degrade silently, not with an error.** `start`/`end` are read with no validation; an omitted or malformed value just makes the comparison permanently false rather than returning a 400. | [availability.ts:11-12](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-ts/src/routes/availability.ts:11). |

Net effect: C1–C3 alone can hide the majority of real conflicts the data actually contains, in different ways, for different bookings — "equipment that looks available but isn't" is not a hypothetical risk here, it's the default behavior of the current code against the current data.

### D. Authorization and personal-data exposure

| # | Finding | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | **The bearer token's signature is never verified**, in either backend ([auth.ts:24-26](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-ts/src/auth.ts:24), [auth.go:28-32](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-go/internal/auth/auth.go:28)). Anyone can hand-construct a base64 JSON payload claiming `role: "ops_director", site_ids: ["*"]` and the server accepts it as fact. This is the root cause that makes D2–D4 exploitable by anyone, not just legitimate users. |
| D2 | **No site or role filtering exists on the endpoint at all.** `req.user` is populated but never read by the availability handler in either backend — every authenticated caller sees every site's equipment and bookings, contradicting the subcontractor's stated scope ("needs to see the equipment schedule **for their site**") and every other role's site restriction in `data/users.json`. | Grep confirms `req.user`/`UserFrom(r)` is unused in both `availability.ts` and `availability.go`. |
| D3 | **Full operator PII is returned in the conflict payload**, not just name: `SELECT * FROM operators WHERE operator_id = ?` ([availability.ts:33-34](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-ts/src/routes/availability.ts:33), mirrored in Go) returns phone, email, **date_of_birth, ssn_last4, emergency_contact**, union_local and home_region — the full HR export — to any caller, for any booking, with no field-level restriction. The frontend only *renders* name+phone ([App.tsx:70](Lumen-equipment-challenge/frontend/src/App.tsx:70)), but the raw JSON response carries everything. Combined with D1, this is a forgeable-token path to every operator's SSN fragment and DOB — directly contradicting Priya's stated requirement ("Only people who need it should see it"). |
| D4 | CORS wildcard + credentials, header logging (including the bearer token itself), and stack-trace-on-500 (all cited in §1) compound D1–D3: there's effectively no boundary stopping a forged token, no filtering once past it, and multiple ways the token or internals could leak via logs/errors. |

### E. Resilience

| # | Finding | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | No FleetCare timeout, retry, circuit-breaker, or fallback-to-stale-data behavior exists, because no FleetCare call exists. Lumen's own vendor doc (`services/maintenance-api/README.md:18`) explicitly warns: *"Service is provided on a best-effort basis... expect intermittent errors and must respect rate limits."* The mock models 503s, 2.5-5s slowness, truncated bodies, and 30s hangs — none of which has a defined handling strategy yet. "Decide what 'sensibly' means" (README) is still open. |
| E2 | Malformed `Authorization` headers (no `Bearer` prefix, non-JWT garbage pasted into the frontend's token box) will make `token.split(".")[1]` undefined and `JSON.parse`/`base64url decode` throw, surfacing as an uncaught exception → 500 with a stack trace (per D4), rather than a clean 401. *(Plausible from reading the code; not exercised at runtime this pass — flagged as a hypothesis below.)* |
| E3 | `/healthz` only confirms the process is up, not that SQLite or (eventually) FleetCare are reachable — no real readiness check. |

### F. Data quality (spreadsheet-export messiness)

All counts from the throwaway script, run against `data/*`:

- **4 incompatible date/time formats** across 743 bookings (details in C2); none mixes formats within its own start/end pair (0 rows), but formats vary row-to-row.
- **75 bookings (10.1%)** have an `asset_tag` that doesn't exact-match any `equipment.csv` row (35 case, 24 whitespace, 16 hyphen-stripped).
- **41 bookings** have notes mentioning cancellation (`"CANCELLED?"`) while `status` still says `confirmed` or `tentative` — the data itself doesn't agree with itself on whether these are live.
- **211 of 743 bookings (28.4%)** have no `operator_id` at all; **106** of those are on cert-required equipment.
- **Cert expiry dates**: 115 entries across 40 operators — 75 in ISO (`YYYY-MM-DD`), 40 in US (`MM/DD/YYYY`) — and **26 of 40 operators (65%) mix both formats within the same `certifications` field.**
- **`booked_by` is free text, not a foreign key**: only 8 distinct values across 743 bookings and 9 users (`"Dana W."`, `"Greg H."`, `"Hector"`, `"aisha"`, `"office"`, plus 3 full names) — no reliable way to attribute a booking to a `user_id` for audit or permission purposes as the data stands.
- **`data/sites.csv` and `data/users.json` disagree on staffing**: `sites.csv` lists Greg Holloway as superintendent of S06/S07, but **no user account for him exists** in `users.json` at all. Separately, `sites.csv` lists Aisha Grant as superintendent of S09/S10, but `users.json` gives her `role: "foreman"` for those same two sites — a direct role contradiction between the two source files for the same person.
- **2 real timezones** (`America/New_York` ×10 sites, `America/Chicago` ×2 — Nashville, S11/S12), and **144 of 743 bookings (19.4%)** are at those two Chicago-timezone sites, where naive-timestamp interpretation isn't a theoretical concern.
- No duplicate `booking_id`s, no bookings referencing retired equipment, no `end <= start` rows, and every `required_cert` value on equipment is held by at least one operator — these are the things that turned out to be *clean*.

### G. Accessibility

| # | Finding | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | Global focus ring removal: `*:focus { outline: none; }` — no visible focus state anywhere, a severe keyboard-navigation failure. | [styles.css:2](Lumen-equipment-challenge/frontend/src/styles.css:2) |
| G2 | Pinch-zoom disabled: `maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no` — directly works against Marcus's stated phone-with-gloves usage. | [index.html:5](Lumen-equipment-challenge/frontend/index.html:5) |
| G3 | "Log out" and each equipment card are `<div onClick>` with no `role`, `tabIndex`, or keyboard handler — not reachable or operable via keyboard/screen reader. | [App.tsx:54,61](Lumen-equipment-challenge/frontend/src/App.tsx:54) |
| G4 | Availability is signaled primarily by a colored dot (green/red) with no text or icon fallback for colorblind users. | [App.tsx:62](Lumen-equipment-challenge/frontend/src/App.tsx:62) |
| G5 | `<select>`/`<input>` filter controls have no associated `<label>`. | [App.tsx:47,52-53](Lumen-equipment-challenge/frontend/src/App.tsx:47) |
| G6 | No loading, empty, or error state exists at all — a failed or slow fetch just leaves the last-rendered (or blank) list with no feedback, which also fails the Part 1 requirement directly. | [App.tsx:21-28](Lumen-equipment-challenge/frontend/src/App.tsx:21) |

### H. Maintainability

- Zero schema constraints of any kind (§1.4) — every invariant (uniqueness, referential integrity, valid status/enum values) is enforced nowhere, which is also the structural reason C1–C4 and B1–B2 are possible.
- The TS and Go backends are hand-kept-in-sync duplicates with identical logic and identical bugs — confirms the "pick one" instruction is the right call, and that the previous contractor's choice to build both in parallel added maintenance cost without reducing risk.
- `DB_PATH`/`REPO_ROOT` are independently re-implemented in three places (`backend-ts/src/env.ts`, `backend-go/internal/config/config.go`, `scripts/lib.mjs`) with slightly different `.env`-parsing logic (quote-stripping only in `scripts/lib.mjs:14`).

---

## 5. Ambiguous or contradictory business rules

| Rule | Tension | What the repo currently does | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Tentative bookings** | Dana: *"tentative bookings shouldn't block anything."* Marcus: *"if I put a tentative on the crane... don't let somebody take it out from under me."* These are mutually exclusive as stated. | Currently blocks on **every** status including `cancelled` (§C4) — not a deliberate resolution of either view, just a missing filter. | **Business decision needed.** A split (tentative blocks *display* as "pending" but allows a second tentative; only a *confirmed* booking blocks another confirm) is one resolution, but that's a design call, not something in the data. |
| **Half-day minimum between sites** | Marcus: *"you can't move a crane across town in zero minutes... half a day between sites, minimum."* | No transit/buffer concept exists anywhere — `bookings` has one `site_id` per row, no "moving from/to," no distance/yard data, no buffer field. | **Business decision needed**, and underspecified even once decided: is "half a day" 12 calendar hours, or half of a defined working day (e.g. 5h of a 7am–5pm day)? Also: does the rule apply to *any* site change, or only certain equipment classes (cranes vs. a skid steer)? |
| **Role/site permissions** | README's role table is deliberately vague ("manages everything," "manages... for them," "requests or books," "oversees... company-wide," "needs to see"). | Not enforced at all today (§D2). One concrete hint exists outside the README: `data/foreman_messages.jsonl:7` (`m07`) explicitly annotates that a subcontractor's request should be "routed to superintendent, not booked" — i.e. **view-only for subcontractors** seems to be the intended answer, just not stated in README's role table. | **Partially answered by data, not by README — worth confirming with Lumen rather than assuming it generalizes (e.g. is `safety_manager`'s `site_ids: ["*"]` meant to also grant booking visibility, or only cert oversight?).** |
| **What counts as "active" for conflict purposes** | Tied to the tentative question above. Also: 41 bookings say "CANCELLED?" in notes while `status` disagrees (§F). | Code treats all three statuses identically. Notes-vs-status disagreement is unresolved in the data itself. | **Business decision** (which statuses block) **+ data cleanup decision** (trust `status`, or treat ambiguous notes as a signal to flag for human review rather than silently trusting either field). |
| **Date/timezone semantics** | Maintenance windows are explicit UTC (`services/maintenance-api/windows.json`). Bookings are naive, in 4 formats, with no timezone marker, across 2 real site timezones (America/New_York vs. America/Chicago, 144 bookings/19.4% at the Chicago sites). | Nothing currently interprets a naive timestamp as site-local vs. UTC vs. anything else — it's raw string comparison. | **Business/data decision needed**: are naive timestamps meant to be site-local wall-clock time (most likely, given they come from a shared spreadsheet humans typed into)? That assumption needs to be stated and then migrated, not inferred per-request. |
| **Certification expiry mid-booking** | Priya: *"if someone's cert expires in the middle of a booking, that's an OSHA problem."* | No code checks this today (Part 2 doesn't exist yet). Data-wise, cert expiry parsing has to handle two formats mixed within a single operator's record 65% of the time (§F). | Not a contradiction, but a concrete requirement with a nontrivial data-parsing prerequisite that should be sized into the Part 2 estimate. |

---

## 6. Confirmed facts vs. runtime hypotheses vs. business questions

**Confirmed by reading code/data (no runtime execution needed to be sure):**
- JWT signature is never verified, both backends (D1).
- SQL injection via unescaped `type` concatenation, both backends (textbook pattern — string concatenation of a raw query param into a SQL string, [availability.ts:16](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-ts/src/routes/availability.ts:16) / [availability.go:21](Lumen-equipment-challenge/backend-go/internal/handlers/availability.go:21)). I did not fire a live injection request this pass (see below).
- No site/role filtering in the availability handler (D2).
- Full-row operator PII returned via `SELECT *` (D3).
- Containment-vs-overlap bug, exact-match asset-tag join, raw string date comparison, missing status filter (C1–C4) — all confirmed directly in source, and C2/C3's real-world impact confirmed against the actual `data/bookings.csv` and `data/equipment.csv` contents via the throwaway script.
- All §F data-quality counts — computed directly, not sampled.
- `seed.mjs` performs no normalization, so these data issues reach the SQLite DB unchanged.

**Hypotheses that would need the app actually running to fully verify** (I did not start any servers or install dependencies this pass, to stay within "reconnaissance only, don't touch files"):
- That a live SQL-injection request against `type=` actually returns attacker-influenced rows or a DB error (code shape makes this near-certain, but unexecuted).
- E2: that a malformed/garbage pasted token actually throws into the generic error handler and returns a 500 with a stack trace, rather than some other failure mode.
- Exact behavior of `node:sqlite` vs. `modernc.org/sqlite` under concurrent writes (relevant to Part 2/3A, not yet applicable since no write endpoint exists).
- Whether the FleetCare mock's chaos percentages produce the described behavior in practice over a real run (the code reads as described; I didn't run it against a client this pass).

**Questions that need a Lumen business decision, not more code reading** (collected from §5): tentative-vs-confirmed blocking semantics; definition and scope of the half-day transit buffer; whether subcontractors (and others) are view-only, confirmed company-wide by role, or something else; how to resolve notes-vs-status disagreement on cancellation; whether naive booking timestamps should be treated as site-local time; and the two staffing-data contradictions (Greg Holloway has no account; Aisha Grant's role conflicts between `sites.csv` and `users.json`) — those last two are really "tell Lumen their HR/roster export doesn't match their site list," not something I can resolve by assumption.

---

Stopping here — no code, data, or doc files were modified, per the brief. Ready for Part 0's plan-writing step whenever you want to move into it.

Now establish runtime evidence before proposing fixes.

Follow the repository's documented setup. Run the existing tests and record their baseline results before changing application behavior. Start the FleetCare mock and exercise both backend implementations sequentially against the same seeded data.

Use the documented token-generation process for representative ops-director, superintendent, foreman, and subcontractor accounts. Keep tokens in shell variables, do not print them, and avoid committing or exposing raw server logs that could contain authorization headers.

Run representative requests covering:
- Valid and invalid query parameters.
- Overlapping bookings, bookings that contain the requested window, bookings contained within it, and partial overlaps at either boundary.
- Adjacent non-overlapping windows.
- Confirmed, tentative, and cancelled bookings.
- Equipment with and without a required operator certification.
- Users with broad access and users restricted to one or more sites.
- Equipment with maintenance windows that intersect the requested dates.
- Equipment with no maintenance windows.
- FleetCare failure, rate limiting, slow responses, and malformed responses where reproducible.

Use CHAOS=off for a predictable functional baseline. For degraded-mode experiments, use the mock's documented deterministic chaos controls or controlled test doubles, bounded request timeouts, and recorded response evidence. Do not assume a request encountered a failure merely because chaos was enabled. Do not modify the vendor mock.

For each backend, record:
1. The exact command and request scenario.
2. The observed HTTP status and relevant sanitized response fields.
3. The database rows or source data that establish the expected result.
4. Whether observed behavior matches the README's requirements and stakeholder statements.
5. Any behavioral difference between TypeScript and Go for the same scenario.
6. Any test or execution environment that prevented verification.

Do not fix anything yet. Produce a reproducible evidence report and update the ranked problem register only when new evidence warrants it.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Throwaway evidence-gathering script. Not part of the repo. Does not print tokens
# or raw server logs. Extracts only sanitized JSON fields from responses.
set -uo pipefail
cd /Users/sammy/Git/RTSLabs/Lumen-equipment-challenge

BASE_URL="$1"
OUT="$2"
: > "$OUT"

log() { echo "$1" | tee -a "$OUT" >/dev/null; echo "$1"; }

OPS_TOKEN=$(npm run -s token -- u-ops-01)

req() {
  local label="$1" qs="$2" token="$3"
  local status body
  body=$(curl -s --max-time 8 -w '\n%{http_code}' "$BASE_URL/api/equipment/availability?$qs" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $token")
  status=$(echo "$body" | tail -1)
  body=$(echo "$body" | sed '$d')
  {
    echo "### $label"
    echo "GET /api/equipment/availability?$qs"
    echo "HTTP $status"
    if echo "$body" | jq -e . >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "$body" | jq -c '.data[]? | {asset_tag, type, available, conflict: (.conflict | if . then {booking_id, site_id, start_at, end_at, status, operator_fields: (.operator | if . then keys else null end)} else null end)}' 2>/dev/null | head -20
      echo "(total items: $(echo "$body" | jq '.data | length' 2>/dev/null))"
    else
      echo "RAW (non-JSON or error), first 300 chars:"
      echo "$body" | head -c 300
      echo ""
    fi
    echo ""
  } >> "$OUT"
}

log "=== Scenarios against $BASE_URL ==="

req "1. No token" "type=mobile_crane&start=2026-10-13&end=2026-10-15" ""
req "2. Malformed garbage token" "type=mobile_crane&start=2026-10-13&end=2026-10-15" "not.a.jwt"
req "3. Baseline (existing test scenario)" "type=mobile_crane&start=2026-10-13&end=2026-10-15" "$OPS_TOKEN"
req "4. SQL injection attempt in type" "type=mobile_crane%27%20OR%20%271%27%3D%271&start=2026-10-13&end=2026-10-15" "$OPS_TOKEN"
req "5. Missing start/end" "type=mobile_crane" "$OPS_TOKEN"
req "6. Booking CONTAINED WITHIN query (control, MC-007/BK-1119 Nov12)" "type=mobile_crane&start=2026-11-10%2000:00&end=2026-11-14%2000:00" "$OPS_TOKEN"
req "7. Query CONTAINED WITHIN booking (bug case, MC-007/BK-1005 Nov15-25)" "type=mobile_crane&start=2026-11-20%2000:00&end=2026-11-22%2000:00" "$OPS_TOKEN"
req "8. Partial overlap, query ends mid-booking (MC-007/BK-1119)" "type=mobile_crane&start=2026-11-12%2000:00&end=2026-11-12%2010:00" "$OPS_TOKEN"
req "9. Partial overlap, query starts mid-booking (MC-007/BK-1119)" "type=mobile_crane&start=2026-11-12%2010:00&end=2026-11-12%2023:59" "$OPS_TOKEN"
req "10. Adjacent non-overlap BEFORE (touches booking start)" "type=mobile_crane&start=2026-11-12%2000:00&end=2026-11-12%2007:30" "$OPS_TOKEN"
req "11. Adjacent non-overlap AFTER (touches booking end)" "type=mobile_crane&start=2026-11-12%2017:00&end=2026-11-12%2020:00" "$OPS_TOKEN"
req "12. Cancelled booking (MC-007/BK-1368 Nov1-6, query inside it)" "type=mobile_crane&start=2026-11-02%2000:00&end=2026-11-04%2000:00" "$OPS_TOKEN"
req "13. Tentative booking (MC-007/BK-1117 Jan1-3 2027, query inside it)" "type=mobile_crane&start=2027-01-01%2000:00&end=2027-01-03%2000:00" "$OPS_TOKEN"
req "14. Whitespace tag + date-only format (EX-009 /BK-1360 Oct4-14)" "type=excavator&start=2026-10-06&end=2026-10-10" "$OPS_TOKEN"
